title: Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD): Simulating Fluid Flow
summary: What is CFD? Simulating Fluid Flow

scenes.title: What is CFD? Simulating Fluid Flow
scenes.narration: Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) uses computers to simulate how liquids and gases move, predicting complex behaviors. This digital approach saves billions in physical testing, accelerating innovation across industries.

scenes.title: Discretization: Breaking Down Flow
scenes.narration: CFD divides a continuous fluid domain into millions of tiny, discrete cells, forming a computational mesh. This process, called discretization, transforms complex physics into solvable algebraic equations for each cell.

scenes.title: Governing Equations: The Physics
scenes.narration: For every cell, CFD solves fundamental governing equations: conservation of mass, momentum (Navier-Stokes), and energy. These complex partial differential equations are numerically approximated to predict fluid velocity, pressure, and temperature.

scenes.title: Aircraft Aerodynamics: Real Example
scenes.narration: In aerospace, CFD is vital for optimizing aircraft aerodynamics, simulating airflow over wings and fuselages. Engineers can virtually test countless designs, reducing drag by up to 15% and significantly improving fuel efficiency before physical prototypes are built.

scenes.title: CFD's Broad Impact & Future
scenes.narration: CFD's impact spans from climate modeling and urban planning to biomedical engineering, enabling predictive insights into complex systems. It continues to drive innovation, helping solve critical challenges and shaping our future designs.
